snippet.title: HTML Headings: h1 to h6 Explained in 60 Seconds
snippet.description:
Use h1 to h6 to organize a page into meaningful sections. See the heading hierarchy with a beginner HTML example.

Which heading would you use for a section inside your page: h1 or h2?

Next lesson: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NwK_T8Qxams
Full beginner course: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEJDqf_3IqMU

H one is the highest heading level; H six is the lowest.
Use heading levels to describe the hierarchy of your content.

Try it: Create a page title and a heading for its first section.


Web Development in 60 Seconds • Lesson 3
Learn more: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Structuring_content

snippet.title: HTML Forms for Beginners: Build Your First Form
snippet.description:
Learn how an HTML form groups input controls, and try a simple beginner form example.

What would your first form collect: feedback or a sign-up?

Next lesson: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MEEDwR24JOw
Full beginner course: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEJDqf_3IqMU

Give controls labels so people can understand what to enter.
The name attribute identifies a field when form data is submitted.

Try it: Create a labeled email field and a submit button.


Web Development in 60 Seconds • Lesson 14
Learn more: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Structuring_content

snippet.title: CSS Box Model: Content, Padding, Border and Margin
snippet.description:
Understand the CSS box model with a visual example of content, padding, border and margin.

Which adds space inside the border: padding or margin?

Next lesson: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_k9pL5fcolg
Full beginner course: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEJDqf_3IqMU

From inside out, it has content, padding, border, and margin.
Padding is inside the border; margin is outside it.

Try it: Give a card padding, a border, and outside margin.


Web Development in 60 Seconds • Lesson 26
Learn more: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Styling_basics

snippet.title: CSS Backgrounds: Make a Two-Color Gradient Card
snippet.description:
Learn CSS backgrounds with a beginner example, then give a card a two-color gradient. Keep text readable over the background.

Full beginner course: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEJDqf_3IqMU

Start with a solid color, or combine colors in a gradient.
A background image can be sized and positioned separately.

snippet.title: CSS Class vs ID: Which Should You Use?
snippet.description:
Compare CSS classes and IDs with a beginner code example. Reuse a class across elements and keep each ID unique.

To style three matching cards, would you choose a class or an ID?

Next lesson: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tozXzYirna4
Full beginner course: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEJDqf_3IqMU

A dot selects a class; a hash selects an identifier.
Reuse a class to apply the same style to several elements.

Try it: Style two elements with one shared class.


Web Development in 60 Seconds • Lesson 27
Learn more: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Styling_basics

snippet.title: CSS Display: Block vs Inline vs Inline-Block
snippet.description:
See how block, inline and inline-block affect a CSS layout. Compare a block container with inline-block labels.

Which display value lets a label flow inline and accept width and height?

Next lesson: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c_JdeG3Iq3o
Full beginner course: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEJDqf_3IqMU

Block elements normally start a new line; inline elements flow with text.
Inline block boxes flow inline while accepting width and height.

Try it: Compare a block container with two inline block labels.


Web Development in 60 Seconds • Lesson 28
Learn more: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Styling_basics

snippet.title: AI: Friend or Devil? The Choice Is Yours | TECH AT 60 #Shorts
snippet.description:
AI can help you learn, practise and draft ideas. But a confident answer can still be wrong. Check important claims, verify urgent requests independently, and think before sharing private information.

Where would you draw the line? Tell us in the comments.

Follow TECH AT 60 for beginner-friendly technology lessons.

#ArtificialIntelligence #AIAwareness #TechAt60 #Shorts
